guidelines.detail: refines GW-06 (The description supports conditional routes for events and milestones during work and optional actions after completion. The missing flows show these routes were not fully represented. This refines GW-06 by covering when to connect the conditional outcomes and how to model a wait for a trigger, consistent with EVT-03.)

same as LRN-020 (The label pairs show semantic differences, while the description supplies actions and qualifiers that can guide faithful labels. This wording is not tied to the specific process and is already substantially covered by learned guideline LRN-020.)

documentation rule LANE-01 not applied (The description distinguishes the player's preference-setting from the bot's farming, while the reference places them in separate lanes. The cited records show that those reference lanes and associated elements have no counterpart in the generated model. Documented guideline LANE-01 already says to use lanes for stated roles or systems, so this guideline restates it.)
same as LRN-020 (The label pairs show task labels changing or narrowing the actions and objects supported by the description. LRN-020 already expresses essentially the same preservation principle.)

refines LANE-01 (The description distinguishes players from the bot that performs farming, while the records show the reference lanes and related start event and task have no counterpart in the generated model. This guideline specifies how to apply LANE-01 when a human and an assisting automated system share one process.)

documentation rule GW-06 not applied (The description allows either or both follow-up actions, while the recorded flow shows the inclusive gateway transition is absent. GW-06 already advises an inclusive split when one or more conditions can be true, so this guideline applies that documented rule to optional follow-up choices.)

same as LRN-020 (The label pairs show activity labels that substitute a different action or alter meaningful details. The description clarifies the relevant urgency, dependencies, and update behavior; LRN-020 already captures the same principle of preserving meaningful details in labels.)

same as LRN-067 (The description distinguishes the player’s preferences from the bot’s farming, supporting separate responsibility lanes. The missing-lane records identify the corresponding modeling difference. This guideline is already covered by learned guideline LRN-067.)

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says that an event or milestone can change the route during work, or that completion makes follow-up actions available: Model the supported outcomes as connected conditional branches, using a suitable gateway for the stated choice; when flow waits for an event or other trigger, model the wait with an intermediate catch event.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that an event or milestone can change the route during work, or that completion makes follow-up actions available

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description distinguishes an event or activity by its action, actor, object, recipient, or another meaningful qualifier: Label each BPMN element so that it preserves those stated details without substituting a broader or different meaning.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description names an activity or outcome and includes meaningful qualifiers about its action, object, recipient, or priority

rules_sent_back.instruction: Use lanes to partition one process by a stated role, department, system or responsibility; lanes are not separate processes.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description assigns different responsibilities within one process to distinct roles, systems, or agents

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description says a person must choose or specify inputs before automated work begins.: Model that choice or specification as a user task before the automated work.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says a person must choose or specify inputs before automated work begins.

rules_sent_back.instruction: When the description assigns work within one process to both a human user and an automated system acting for that user.: Use separate lanes to show their respective responsibilities and assign each described activity to the responsible lane.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description assigns work within one process to both a human user and an automated system acting for that user.

rules_sent_back.instruction: Use an inclusive split when one or more conditions can be true; use an inclusive join to synchronize only activated reachable branches.
rules_sent_back.situation: the description says that, after a process outcome, one or more optional follow-up actions can be selected, including several at once
